checked_sources.source: Tinu Theckel Joy, Santu Rana, Sunil Gupta, Svetha Venkatesh, A flexible transfer learning framework for Bayesian optimization with convergence guarantee, Expert Systems with Applications 115 (2019) 656-672, DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2018.08.023
checked_sources.result: Envelope-BO models source observations as target observations with learned extra source-noise. When tasks are unrelated the inferred source noise can become arbitrarily large, effectively ignoring source data and rolling back to generic target-only BO. Experiments include same- and different-distribution transfer. Reported CPU seconds to best performance (Envelope-BO vs Generic-BO) include Elastic Net mushrooms 55.65 vs 131.37, madelon 90.87 vs 193.12, a8a 1132.05 vs 1758.59; SVM mushrooms 43.25 vs 97.14, madelon 51.32 vs 240.3, a8a 1353.17 vs 2031.81; MLP MNIST 4256.43 vs 11855.69.

checked_sources.source: Shubhada Agrawal, Sandeep Juneja, Peter Glynn, Optimal delta-Correct Best-Arm Selection for Heavy-Tailed Distributions, ALT 2020, PMLR 117:61-110
checked_sources.result: Proves a critical negative result: without restrictions on unbounded-support arm distributions, any delta-correct best-arm procedure can require infinite expected samples. Under a known bound on a nonnegative increasing convex moment functional (e.g. a bounded squared moment), the proposed algorithm is delta-correct and asymptotically matches the information-theoretic lower bound as delta goes to zero. The paper also introduces batching because repeatedly solving its max-min allocation problem is computationally expensive; the paper reports individual solve times of roughly 35, 69, 135 and 192 minutes after 2k, 5k, 10k and 20k samples on the stated desktop setup and shows a nontrivial near-optimal batch-size regime.

checked_sources.source: Tianyuan Wu et al., Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes, arXiv:2604.28138 (2026)
checked_sources.result: Resolved the prior checkpoint-classification-error frontier. Manual labels over 2,063 turns from 100 iFlow-cli Terminal-Bench tasks show zero false negatives for both process and filesystem changes; process detection was 100% accurate; filesystem detection was 98.3% accurate with 2.3% false positives and zero false negatives. The false positives are conservative over-approximation and only trigger an extra filesystem checkpoint. Across workloads Crab keeps 100% recovery correctness, skips at least 70% and up to 87% of checkpoints, and stays within 0-1.9% of no-fault execution time under the tested crash setup.

checked_sources.source: Siyang Gao et al., Robust ranking and selection with optimal computing budget allocation, Automatica 81 (2017) 30-36
checked_sources.result: Extends OCBA to input uncertainty represented by multiple plausible scenarios and selects according to worst-case performance. The procedure reallocates budget across design-scenario pairs instead of assuming a single perfectly known input distribution. The accessible primary text confirms significant numerical-efficiency gains but this run did not recover exact table values, so no new numeric speedup claim is made.

checked_sources.source: Ben Liblit et al., Public Deployment of Cooperative Bug Isolation / CBI materials
checked_sources.type: primary deployment paper and project materials
checked_sources.result: Rechecked sparse telemetry branch. Public CBI uses randomized sparse predicate sampling (e.g. 1/100 in deployment) to aggregate weak per-run observations across many runs; source material reports no user performance complaints at that rate and earlier experiments show low-overhead sparse sampling. This run did not recover a clean inspected-lines or diagnosis-time reduction endpoint versus dense tracing, so the branch remains open rather than being promoted on weak evidence.

candidates_new.mechanism: Treat prior-task observations as uncertain target observations and infer their transfer noise/relatedness from target evidence. As inferred mismatch grows, continuously downweight source information; when source and target are effectively unrelated, ignore source data and revert to the target-only optimizer rather than forcing transfer.
candidates_new.primary_source: Joy et al., Expert Systems with Applications 115 (2019), DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2018.08.023
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: The primary preprint's CPU-time table reports time-to-best-performance for Envelope-BO versus Generic-BO: Elastic Net mushrooms 55.65 vs 131.37 s, madelon 90.87 vs 193.12 s, a8a 1132.05 vs 1758.59 s; SVM mushrooms 43.25 vs 97.14 s, madelon 51.32 vs 240.3 s, a8a 1353.17 vs 2031.81 s; MLP MNIST 4256.43 vs 11855.69 s. The paper also evaluates different source/target data distributions and states that learned source noise causes unrelated source observations to be ignored, recovering generic BO.
candidates_new.operational_observable: Maintain a learned source-to-target discrepancy/noise variable from observed target residuals. Gate source influence by this discrepancy rather than a fixed trust flag. Define a hard safety fallback: if inferred source noise exceeds the scale at which source observations materially change the posterior/acquisition, run target-only optimization.
candidates_new.scope: Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization with the paper's proximity/noise model and tested ML hyperparameter tasks. The fallback is principled within that model; it is not a universal proof against every form of negative transfer or adversarial source data.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Any reuse of historical experiments, proxy tasks, prior domains or previous configurations should carry an explicit learned transfer weight plus a target-only fallback. Past evidence should accelerate cold start only while current observations empirically support relatedness.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source-domain mechanism and tested fallback behavior; medium-high for broader experimental scheduler transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Before trusting mean/variance-based candidate allocation, detect whether evaluation outcomes lie in a light-tail regime that supports ordinary plug-in estimators. For heavy-tailed or unbounded outcomes, require an explicit tail/moment constraint and use robust best-arm statistics; otherwise a fixed-confidence guarantee may have infinite expected sampling cost.
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: The strongest result is structural rather than a single benchmark speedup: without distributional restrictions, delta-correct best-arm identification over unbounded-support distributions can require infinite expected samples. Under a known bound on a suitable convex moment functional, their procedure asymptotically matches the lower bound as delta tends to zero. The implementation also reveals allocation-computation cost severe enough that one max-min solve after 2k/5k/10k/20k samples took about 35/69/135/192 minutes on the reported desktop, motivating near-optimal batching.
candidates_new.operational_observable: Track empirical tail diagnostics and a declared/validated moment bound for each candidate's outcome distribution. If the tail contract is absent or violated, do not interpret variance/gap allocation formulas as confidence guarantees; switch to robust mean/best-arm machinery or cap the claim to heuristic ranking. Separately choose allocation-recompute batch size by total compute cost, not sample efficiency alone.
candidates_new.scope: Fixed-confidence best-arm identification with heavy-tailed distributions and known moment-type constraint. This does not directly solve nonstationary drift or correlated arms; it supplies a failure boundary and robust replacement class for one major violation of classical OCBA assumptions.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Evaluation pipelines should make tail-regime validation a prerequisite for aggressive evidence concentration. Rare catastrophic outcomes can invalidate ordinary sample-mean confidence, so the scheduler needs an explicit heavy-tail mode rather than silently overtrusting empirical variance.
candidates_new.confidence: high for impossibility/robust-identification result; medium-high for scheduler guardrail transfer

evidence_updates.update: The safe-transfer frontier now has a concrete target-only fallback mechanism and matched timing evidence from Joy et al. Source task information is not merely cost-weighted; its influence is continuously reduced by learned source noise, and unrelated source data is ignored so optimization reverts to generic BO. This materially strengthens the prior requirement that source/proxy reuse must be able to disable itself under mismatch.

Crab's primary paper provides the previously missing classification-error audit: 2,063 manually labeled turns, zero false negatives for process and filesystem changes, 100% process accuracy, 98.3% filesystem accuracy, 2.3% filesystem false positives. The observed safe bias is conservative false positives, which cost extra cheap filesystem checkpoints rather than corrupt recovery.

Heavy-tail literature establishes a hard regime boundary absent from normal/variance plug-in OCBA/DAA: with unrestricted unbounded-support outcomes, fixed-confidence best-arm selection may require infinite expected samples. Therefore any deployment of gap/variance allocation should label its tail assumptions and fail over to robust heavy-tail identification when those assumptions are not supported.

frontier: Find a robust fixed-budget or fixed-confidence ranking-and-selection method for correlated observations/common random numbers with explicit quantitative gain or failure relative to independent-allocation OCBA; extract the covariance observable that should enter allocation.

Extend heavy-tail guardrails to nonstationary evaluation drift: look for best-arm/ranking-selection procedures with change detection, forgetting windows, or piecewise-stationary guarantees, and quantify the cost of stale evidence.

Search safe-transfer BO/experimental design under deliberately misleading or adversarial source tasks, preferring papers that measure negative-transfer frequency/regret and demonstrate a target-only fallback in the same experiment.
Search sequential wet-lab model discrimination with a random/uniform/nonadaptive baseline experiment count; quantify samples saved and identify misspecification/model-set expansion triggers.

Find statistical-debugging or fault-localization primary studies reporting diagnosis latency, inspected-code reduction, or runs-to-localize under sparse sampling versus dense/adaptive tracing; use failure rarity to derive a telemetry-density regime switch.

For semantics-aware checkpointing, seek adversarial workload shifts or classifier blind spots beyond the 2,063-turn audit, especially unobserved kernel/device/network state where zero false negatives on the tested filesystem/process labels may not transfer.
